newsitem.title: USA: Natgas futures end higher with cash, storm threat.
newsitem.headline: Natgas futures end higher with cash, storm threat.

text.p: NYMEX Henry Hub natgas futures wavered only slightly this afternoon to settle higher as cash buyers stuffed gas into storage in anticipation of Hurricane Hortense, which still poses a potential threat to the Gulf, industry sources said Monday.
October settled 3.5 cents firmer at $1.898 per million British thermal units. November ended up 6.6 cents at $2.123, pushing the Oct/Nov spread to 22.5 cents.
Despite an early futures rally, the October trading range remain tight from $1.855 to $1.91.

At 1400 EDT, Hortense was about 130 miles southeast of Ponce, Puerto Rico, and packing winds as high as 80 miles per hour. The storm, which comes in the wake of Fran, is moving in a west to west-northwest direction.

Cash prices on the U.S. Gulf Coast pipes were at least five cents higher in the mid-$1.70s to low-$1.80s. Midcontinent prices were also firmer in the low-to-mid $1.60s, while the Permian basin market surged into the high-$1.50s to mid-$1.60s.
Technically, October support was still seen at $1.84. The next floors were pegged at $1.80, $1.735 and $1.68. Resistance was seen first in the low-$1.90s, then $1.955.
NYMEX said an estimated 30,401 Henry Hub contracts traded, up from Friday's revised tally of 22,086. The 12-month strip rose 4.3 cents to $2.061.
NYMEX's October Permian contract remained steady throughout the day, settling 2.5 cents higher at $1.575. NYMEX said an estimated 26 lots exchanged hands.
On the KCBT, October finished up 4.7 cents at $1.66. The East/West spread widened by 2.8 cents to 23.8 cents (NYMEX premium).
